basis: The document's own copyright paragraph, under its header: "Copyright © 2011-2013 W3C® (MIT, ERCIM, Keio, Beihang), All Rights Reserved. W3C liability, trademark and document use rules apply", where 'document use' links to http://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/copyright-documents (the W3C Document License; no SPDX id). It permits copying and distributing the document's contents, or portions of them, in any medium for any purpose, provided every copy carries a link to the original, the pre-existing copyright notice, and the document's status; it grants NO right to modify. So this entry holds the text verbatim and changes no wording: the link, notice and status are in its own front-matter sections and repeated in `note`. Splitting it into per-section files is a reading of 'portions' and of 'any medium', recorded here so the owner can overrule it (issue #1614).
note: Source: the W3C Working Group's own publication snapshot of the Recommendation, github.com/w3c/prov at commit aa82bd71b6bb1f7b735bf3f7f5b948fae87764f0, path ontology/releases/REC-prov-o-20130430/Overview.html (last changed there in 4e0e1213b786e06f77162fad0ff0f10582aa0d75, 2013-04-23). Its status section and header read 'W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013', 'This version: http://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-o-20130430/'. It is therefore the REC text as the WG staged it for publication, NOT an editor's draft; w3.org is unreachable from the ingesting container, so it was not compared byte for byte with the copy at http://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-o-20130430/. Printed to PDF offline (headless Chromium 141, network blocked, document outline from the headings), then ingested with the pdf-structure rung. Styles and the W3C logo, which load from w3.org, are absent from the print; the text and the repository-local figures are not. Errata published after the REC are not included.
